description: Affine (12 degrees of freedom) registration of a moving volume to a template with niimath -allineate, Chris Rorden's C port of AFNI 3dAllineate from the lightNIIng project (CPU, seconds per T1). Writes the moving image resampled onto the template grid and the affine as a JSON matrix that -applymat can replay on other images. Register a skull-stripped image to a skull-stripped template, or a full-head image to a full-head template.

moving.description: Image to register (NIfTI). A 4D image is registered by its first volume.

template.description: Fixed reference image, e.g. MNI152 T1 1 mm (brain-only when the moving image is skull-stripped).

cost.description: Cost function: fast (default; hel+cr), fastx, fasthel, fastcr, hel, nmi, lpc, lpa, ls.

interpolation.description: Final resampling: NN (label maps), linear, cubic.

weight.description: Optional weight image in template space that restricts the cost function.

registered.description: Moving image resampled onto the template grid.

transform.description: niimath allineate_affine JSON: the 4x4 world-mm matrix (template to moving, plus its inverse), cost, engine and inputs. Replay with niimath <image> -applymat transform.json -master <template> <out>.

block.label: Affine registration (niimath)
block.description: Register to a template with niimath -allineate.

requirements: niimath v1.0.20260924 or newer with -allineate (on PATH, ~/bin, /usr/local/bin, or via NIIMATH)
neuroflow/launch.description: Runs niimath <moving> -allineate <template> -cost <cost> -final <interpolation> [-weight <weight>] -savemat transform.json registered.nii.gz through the shared native CLI adapter.

probe.advice: Install niimath v1.0.20260924 or newer (https://github.com/rordenlab/niimath/releases) and point NIIMATH at it; older builds have no -allineate.

neuroflow/cli.source: https://github.com/rordenlab/niimath (-allineate: lightNIIng spatial_processing port of AFNI 3dAllineate)

useWhen: Affinely register (12 degrees of freedom) an image to a template such as MNI152, getting the resampled image and a replayable transform.
Bring a skull-stripped T1 into MNI space for comparison or reporting.

avoidWhen.when: The moving image is full-head but the template is brain-only: skull-strip it first.
You need nonlinear (deformable) registration: this is affine only.

preconditions: niimath v1.0.20260924 or newer with -allineate, on PATH, in ~/bin or /usr/local/bin, or via NIIMATH.
moving and template are both skull-stripped or both full-head.
effects: Writes registered.nii.gz on the template grid and transform.json (4x4 world-mm affine and its inverse) to the output directory.
Use interpolation NN when the moving image is a label map.

duration.basis: Measured over 9 gallery runs on an Apple-silicon Mac: median 1.3 s for a 1 mm T1 brain to MNI152 1 mm; the slowest took 4.7 s.

examples.title: Brain to the MNI152 brain template

failures.remedy: Install niimath v1.0.20260924 or newer from github.com/rordenlab/niimath/releases, or set NIIMATH to its path.

match.contains: does not look like a usable niimath

failures.meaning: The niimath found is too old: it has no -allineate.
failures.remedy: Install niimath v1.0.20260924 or newer and point NIIMATH at it.
Read the step log, and check both images with neuroflow_inspect.
